browser: The user's stable Google Chrome, driven through the official Claude in Chrome extension in its own tab-group window. Keys were synthetic in-page keydown/keyup events; touch buttons were pointer events on the real touch buttons; Start, language, shift tiles and Play again were real mouse clicks. Only visible DOM text and canvas pixels were read; no game state was read or injected.
phoneLayouts: Checked in a same-origin 390-wide portrait frame on the page.
servedSourceCheck: The SHA-256 of the served src/games/traffic-conductor.js was computed in the page and matched f02a8ca3.

observed: A driver that reads only the status-line prompt played shifts 1 to 20 in English back to back in about 22 minutes and reached 'Nicely played! Every junction is running smoothly - well conducted!' (score 20784) without taking a strike, using 242 key presses including junction selection on the two-junction shifts.
Chinese shift select listed all 20 shifts after the win.

Chinese: idling on shift 3 first took a strike, then lost with the ambulance banner '救护车在东向道路等待超过 3 秒，本班结束！' and the end screen '第 3 班救护车被耽误，你被换下岗位。'; arrow, Space and X on the loss screen changed nothing.

Chinese phone frame, 371 px wide with no horizontal overflow: the touch arrows moved the shift cursor to shift 1, the 信号 button started it, and touch taps alone following the prompt cleared it (20/20, no strikes).
R during shift 2 in the phone frame returned to shift select; Play again on the loss screen also returned to shift select.

limitations: Physical phones, other browsers, tapping junctions on the canvas and audio were not tested. Console output was not captured in this session.
